page.layout: One page of running text in one column; a rule and a chapter heading in the middle; a short paragraph at the foot; notes in the left margin, cropped at the gutter.

main_text.p: nicus,tia quâ in tempore, reipsa, omnes creaturas actu-at & ordinat, prout ab æterno præordinaverat.
1. Quòd decretum & Executio accuratissimè inter se congruant, hæcque illius speculum, illud hujus exemplar.fumma[?]
2. Quod respondeant sibi ordine retrogrado, ita ut primum in intentione, ultimum sit in executione, & vicissim.ie & ne
3. Quòd utrumq; nitatur divinâ omnisuf-ficientiâ, & omniefficientiâ.creatu.
V. Executio est rerum productio vel conser-vatio, ac Gubernatio quò concursus.I non
VI. Productio est actio Dei quâ Deus facit ut omnes creaturæ, omnesq; ipsarum perfectiones primò sint.unica.
Hæc primò est universalissima creatio, & dein formatio quorundam individuorum. In hisce nō valdè opus, ut multum simus prolixi.labit
main_text.head: CAP. XX. De Conservatione.
main_text.p: COnservatio est actio Dei quâ Deus facit ut omnes creaturæ ipsarumque facultates congruè durent.delibe

page.notes: Printed page number 91 sits at the head, between ornaments. No running head is printed. The left margin is cut off at the gutter, so the marginal notes survive only as fragments; the readings there are partly illegible and the fragments shown are approximate. The printed long s (s) appears as f in "Confervatione", "concursus" and similar words; these are rendered as s. The bottom catchword "I. Con-" is printed at the lower right.
